paper.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

read_sources.note: Used for arXiv metadata, current revision, abstract, Nature journal reference, and DOI links.
Read for method details, R1-Zero and R1 pipeline, evaluation summary, distillation, unsuccessful attempts, and limitations.
Used to confirm public model/code release, model family, distillation set, and license notes.

summary.one_sentence: DeepSeek-R1 shows that large-scale reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can elicit long-chain reasoning, then packages the result into a stronger cold-start-plus-RL model and distilled smaller models.
summary.thesis: The paper separates two claims: R1-Zero is the clean experiment that reasoning behaviors can emerge from pure RL on a base model, while R1 is the practical recipe that adds cold-start data, staged RL, rejection sampling, SFT, and alignment RL to make the behavior usable.
summary.why_it_matters: For agents, DeepSeek-R1 made verifiable reward reinforcement learning a concrete infrastructure pattern: if correctness can be checked, post-training can optimize trajectories at scale without hand-labeling every reasoning path.

prior_state: Strong reasoning models relied heavily on supervised demonstrations, preference data, or closed training recipes.
Open post-training stacks lacked a clear frontier-scale example showing reasoning behavior emerging primarily from automatically checkable rewards.
Long chain-of-thought models introduced inference-time scaling, but the training recipe for producing them was not broadly visible.
Agent builders needed evidence for when to use verifiers and reward functions instead of treating reasoning as only prompt engineering.
problem.key_gap: The paper asks whether an LLM can develop stronger reasoning through reinforcement learning against verifiable tasks, and how to turn the emergent but rough behavior into a usable model family.
assumptions: The target tasks have reliable automatic reward signals, especially math, code, and STEM-style answer checking.
A capable base model such as DeepSeek-V3-Base is available.
Longer reasoning traces are acceptable at inference time for harder tasks.
The training setup can afford large-scale rollout generation and reward evaluation.

concepts.name: DeepSeek-R1-Zero
concepts.definition: A model trained from DeepSeek-V3-Base with large-scale reinforcement learning and no supervised fine-tuning cold start.

concepts.name: DeepSeek-R1
concepts.definition: The practical model that adds cold-start data and a multi-stage training pipeline around reasoning-oriented RL.

concepts.name: Group Relative Policy Optimization
concepts.definition: The RL algorithm used by the paper to optimize reasoning behavior without a separate critic in the same style as PPO.

concepts.name: Accuracy reward
concepts.definition: A rule-based reward that checks whether the model's final answer is correct for verifiable tasks.

concepts.name: Format reward
concepts.definition: A reward component that encourages the model to wrap its reasoning in the required think-tag format.

concepts.name: Distilled reasoning model
concepts.definition: A smaller Qwen- or Llama-based model fine-tuned on outputs generated by DeepSeek-R1.

method.core_idea: Use verifiable tasks as the reward source for RL, observe what reasoning behaviors emerge without supervised traces, then add cold-start data and staged post-training to improve readability, language control, general capability, and smaller-model transfer.
action_grammar: prompt: problem statement with instructions to produce reasoning and final answer.
accuracy reward: checker result for the final answer.
format reward: adherence to the required reasoning/answer tags.
GRPO update: policy update using grouped rollout rewards.
cold-start data: thousands of curated examples used before R1's main RL stage.
distillation data: 800K samples generated by DeepSeek-R1.
steps: Train R1-Zero by applying GRPO to DeepSeek-V3-Base on reasoning tasks with rule-based accuracy and format rewards.
Track whether longer reasoning, self-reflection, verification, and strategy adaptation emerge during RL.
For R1, collect thousands of cold-start examples to make initial reasoning traces more readable and controlled.
Run reasoning-oriented RL from the cold-start model.
Use rejection sampling and supervised fine-tuning to broaden the model beyond narrow reasoning tasks.
Run a final RL stage for helpfulness, harmlessness, and all-scenario alignment.
Generate 800K training samples from DeepSeek-R1 and distill reasoning behavior into smaller dense Qwen and Llama models.
method.pseudocode:
base = DeepSeekV3Base()

r1_zero = grpo_train(
    policy=base,
    tasks=verifiable_reasoning_tasks,
    reward=accuracy_reward + format_reward,
)

cold = sft(base, curated_cold_start_reasoning_examples)
reasoner = grpo_train(cold, verifiable_reasoning_tasks, accuracy_reward)
wide = sft(reasoner, rejection_sample(reasoner) + non_reasoning_instruction_data)
r1 = rl_align(wide, helpfulness_reward + harmlessness_reward)

distill_data = sample(r1, count=800000)
distilled_models = [sft(student, distill_data) for student in qwen_and_llama_students]

claims.statement: DeepSeek-R1-Zero demonstrates that reasoning behaviors can emerge from pure large-scale RL on a base model without supervised fine-tuning as a preliminary step.
caveats: R1-Zero is not the final usable model; the paper says it has readability and language-mixing problems.

claims.statement: During R1-Zero training, AIME 2024 pass@1 rises from 15.6% to 71.0%, and majority voting reaches 86.7%.
caveats: This is a math benchmark result, not a general-agent reliability result.

claims.statement: DeepSeek-R1 adds cold-start data and a multi-stage pipeline to fix R1-Zero's practical weaknesses while preserving reasoning RL as the load-bearing mechanism.
caveats: The recipe is no longer a pure-RL result; the practical model uses SFT, rejection sampling, and multiple RL stages.

claims.statement: The paper reports DeepSeek-R1 performance comparable to OpenAI-o1-1217 on reasoning tasks.
caveats: The comparison is benchmark-specific and mostly on reasoning-heavy tasks, not broad tool-use or workflow reliability.

claims.statement: Reasoning behavior transfers to smaller dense models through distillation from DeepSeek-R1 outputs.
caveats: The distilled models inherit a synthetic-data pipeline and are evaluated mainly through benchmark performance, not deployed agent behavior.

claims.statement: The project releases DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1, and six distilled dense models spanning 1.5B to 70B parameters.
caveats: The repository/model licenses vary through underlying Qwen and Llama bases for distilled variants.

claims.statement: The authors state that DeepSeek-R1 still falls short on function calling, multi-turn interaction, complex role-play, JSON output, language mixing outside Chinese and English, prompt sensitivity, and software-engineering RL efficiency.
caveats: These limitations are directly relevant to agent infrastructure and should not be hidden behind headline math/coding scores.

claims.statement: The paper reports unsuccessful attempts with process reward models, Monte Carlo tree search, and related search-style methods in their setting.
caveats: These are negative results for this implementation and scale, not impossibility results for all process rewards or search methods.

evidence.result: The paper describes R1-Zero as trained through large-scale RL without preliminary SFT and reports emergent reasoning behaviors such as self-reflection, verification, and dynamic strategy adaptation.
The paper reports that R1-Zero's AIME 2024 pass@1 increases from 15.6% to 71.0%, and that majority voting improves the score to 86.7%.
DeepSeek-R1 starts from thousands of cold-start examples, then uses reasoning-oriented RL, rejection sampling plus SFT, and a final RL stage for broader helpfulness and harmlessness.
The authors summarize DeepSeek-R1 as achieving performance comparable to OpenAI-o1-1217 across a range of reasoning tasks.

The paper says DeepSeek-R1 generates 800K samples for student fine-tuning, and reports that DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B reaches 28.9% on AIME and 83.9% on MATH, outperforming GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet on those math benchmarks.
The paper and repository state that DeepSeek-R1-Zero, DeepSeek-R1, and six dense distilled models based on Qwen and Llama checkpoints are released, covering 1.5B, 7B, 8B, 14B, 32B, and 70B sizes.

The paper lists weaknesses in function calling, multi-turn tasks, complex role-play, JSON output, non-Chinese/non-English language mixing, few-shot prompt sensitivity, and software-engineering RL because long evaluations slow the RL loop.
The discussion identifies process reward models, Monte Carlo tree search, and related search attempts as unsuccessful or insufficient in the authors' experiments.

agent_infra_takeaways: DeepSeek-R1 turns verifiers into training infrastructure: the key artifact is not a prompt but a reliable reward path for answer checking.
R1-Zero is the clean scientific result; R1 is the productizable recipe. Keep those separate when reasoning about what pure RL achieved.
For agents, RLVR works best where the environment can emit a crisp correctness signal, such as math, code, format, or executable tests.
Long reasoning traces are a serving concern. Better task success may come with higher token budgets, latency, and scheduler pressure.
Distillation turns expensive reasoning models into cheaper student policies, but the quality of the generated trajectories becomes part of the training data contract.
Function calling, JSON output, multi-turn interaction, and software engineering remain weak spots in the paper's own limitation section, so agent builders still need runtime checks.
Prompt sensitivity matters operationally: the paper recommends zero-shot, direct problem statements because few-shot prompting can degrade performance.
caveats: The current arXiv record is v2 revised in January 2026 and also lists a Nature 2025 journal reference; this review treats the arXiv and Nature metadata as the current source record.
R1-Zero's pure-RL result should not be confused with DeepSeek-R1's final multi-stage recipe.
Benchmark parity with OpenAI-o1-1217 is scoped to reasoning tasks reported by the paper.
The evidence is strongest for verifiable reasoning tasks, not open-ended autonomous agents with side effects.
The authors explicitly report limitations in function calling, multi-turn interaction, JSON output, language mixing, prompt sensitivity, and software-engineering RL.
The paper's exact training data and infrastructure details are not fully reproducible from the public text alone.

related_work.title: Tulu 3
related_work.note: Tulu 3 lays out an open post-training recipe where RLVR is one stage; DeepSeek-R1 makes verifiable-reward RL the headline mechanism at frontier reasoning scale.

related_work.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
related_work.note: DeepSeek-R1 optimizes the long reasoning traces that chain-of-thought prompting exposed as useful at inference time.

related_work.title: Self-Consistency
related_work.note: R1-Zero's majority-vote AIME improvement is a direct example of buying reasoning reliability with multiple sampled trajectories.

related_work.title: SWE-bench
related_work.note: The same verifier-first logic becomes agent evaluation infrastructure when correctness is executable through tests.

poc.note: No PoC yet - contributions welcome. A small PoC could train a tiny policy on arithmetic traces with a rule-based answer checker, then compare supervised traces against reward-only updates.
